issues.body: `refresh_prohibition` still builds ambiguous-deny provenance with `naming_prohibition_ids`, and that helper still filters only through `rule_action_target_match`. That predicate intentionally checks action and target only; it does not apply the assignee match or constraint classification used by `prohibition_status`. Consequently, if one rule is genuinely ambiguous while another action/target-identical rule is assignee-mismatched or definitely false under supplied evidence, the retained deny is annotated with both IDs even though the latter cannot be carving out this request. This makes the rule-level audit result incorrect, and none of the added tests exercises this mixed-classification refresh case.
issues.fix_hint: Expose or reuse the evaluator's per-rule three-valued prohibition classification so ambiguous refresh provenance includes only rules classified `Ambiguous` for this request, including assignee and full constraint evaluation. Add a refresh regression test with one ambiguous prohibition and one action/target-identical but definitely-false or assignee-mismatched prohibition, then assert that only the ambiguous rule ID is present.
issues.title: Ambiguous refresh still attributes definitely inapplicable prohibitions

verdict.summary: Round 4's major correctness finding remains unchanged. The ambiguous-refresh path still obtains provenance from `naming_prohibition_ids`, which selects all action/target-compatible prohibitions even though the policy evaluator's classification also considers assignee and each constraint's three-valued result. Thus a retained fail-closed deny can still be annotated with a definitely inapplicable rule. The added provenance tests do not cover an ambiguous prohibition alongside an assignee-mismatched or definitely-false sibling. Progress is stagnant because the same issue remains at the same severity.
